newsitem.title: FRANCE: Albania saga sad, must stop swindlers - Camdessus.
newsitem.headline: Albania saga sad, must stop swindlers - Camdessus.

text.p: IMF chief Michel Camdessus said on Wednesday that he was appalled by the collapse of get rich quick savings funds and the ensuing violence in Albania, but believed this would not stop the country from moving to a market economy.
"It's a catastrophe for the poor people," Camdessus, head of the International Monetary Fund, said on French RFI radio.
"It's appalling. This will cost the country dearly, but this is not the end of Albania's transition to a market economy," he said, according to extracts of his remarks supplied to Reuters by RFI.
Camdessus said that, despite IMF and World Bank warnings, the government had failed to give itself the means to ensure the necessary controls and discipline.
He added that he hoped the necessary measures would be taken to prevent "swindlers stealing public savings" in the future.
